analysis.title: The semi massacre: Goldman sees a major disconnect
key_insights: Texas accounts for more than a quarter of planned US data center capacity additions through 2030, and talk of a potential moratorium has rattled the AI complex.

Goldman argues restrictions on new permits do not stop projects already under construction. The 35 GW of data center additions planned for 2027 are largely already being built, with limited execution risk.
Goldman still sees $1.3 trillion in AI infrastructure capex by 2027.
SOX has had one of its most extreme drawdowns in history. It bounced off its long-term trendline but remains well below the 200-day MA.
Semis positioning has been washed out, with allocations back near year lows. The open question is how fast investors must rebuild exposure if the squeeze continues.
Goldman says that even with zero growth in 2028, NVDA and AVGO trade at 12x and 13x earnings respectively.
AVGO is below its 200-day MA but has bounced off a long-term trendline that has held for years.

Memory has been hit especially hard. Goldman notes Samsung and SK Hynix trade below book value and Micron is approaching historically attractive valuation territory, with free cash flow expected to improve.
MU trades just below its 200-day MA. A close back above it could trigger another round of buying.
JPMorgan highlights SK Hynix at 2.6x 2027 estimated earnings and Samsung at 2.8x. The broader memory group trades at 3.6x despite projected EPS CAGR of 98% for 2026-2028.
JPMorgan notes earnings estimates have not followed share prices lower and sees little risk of cuts over the next six months.
The Market Ear's bottom line: the market is pricing an AI spending collapse while Goldman sees a largely committed construction pipeline. Longer-term oversupply risks remain.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman says NVDA trades at 12x earnings even under a zero-growth 2028 scenario.
Goldman says AVGO trades at 13x earnings under a zero-growth 2028 scenario. The stock is below its 200-day MA but has bounced off a multi-year trendline.
Goldman says Micron is approaching historically attractive valuation territory. It trades just below its 200-day MA.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is washed out, valuations have reset and the data center buildout continues. The report frames the setup as increasingly interesting and a potential bigger squeeze.

earnings_insights: Goldman: under a zero-growth 2028 scenario, NVDA trades at 12x and AVGO at 13x earnings (valuation estimate, not a reported figure).
JPMorgan: memory group projected EPS CAGR of 98% for 2026-2028 (estimate). Earnings estimates have not been cut as shares fell, with little risk of cuts seen over the next six months.
risk_factors: A potential Texas data center moratorium on new permits.
SOX remains well below its 200-day MA and the fundamental debate is unsettled.
vol_and_positioning: Semis positioning has been washed out, with allocations back toward year lows.
SOX has had one of its most extreme drawdowns in history and bounced off its long-term trendline, but remains well below the 200-day MA.
A continued squeeze could force investors to rebuild semis exposure quickly.
cross_bank_references: Goldman on data center buildout and AI valuations, with JPMorgan on Korean memory valuations, cited together in the same note.
